review_notes: I read the whole file. I searched Mathlib for existing Hilbert–Schmidt or Frobenius norms on linear maps between inner product spaces. I also searched for existing basis-independent sums ∑ᵢ ‖A bᵢ‖². The only Frobenius norm I found was the matrix one in Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Normed. The file already uses that one through `Matrix.frobenius_norm_def` in `LinearMap.frobenius_norm_toMatrix`, so it links to it and does not compete with it. The file builds `frobenius` on Mathlib's `PiLp`, `normSeminorm` and `Seminorm.comp`. `LinearMap.trace_adjoint_comp_self_eq_sum_norm_apply_sq` uses Mathlib's `trace_eq_sum_inner`. `sum_norm_apply_sq_eq_sum_norm_apply_sq` is a standalone theorem, which the rubric excludes. Mathlib has no unitarily invariant seminorm structure or Frobenius seminorm on `E →ₗ F`, so no competing definition exists. Tau Ceti has a separate HilbertSchmidt directory (TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/HilbertSchmidt/Basic.lean) that may overlap with this file's concept. I did not read it. It is not Mathlib, so it falls outside this rubric. Remaining uncertainty is limited to that internal overlap.
